_purpose: Executable test cases (EC) for UC1b ('Live' tap-to-reveal) — runnable expansion of the scenarios. Per scenario: 1 success EC + exactly one alternative EC per expected.alternative[] entry.
_id_note: EC- = Executable Case. Chain: AC → SC → EC.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify first tap on a playing Live stream reveals controls without pausing (mobile)
preconditions: a 'Live' stream is playing on a mobile surface
steps: Play a Live stream on mobile with the overlay hidden
Tap anywhere on the player surface
Assert: the controls overlay appears
Assert: video.paused === false (still playing)
Assert: the central button shows the pause icon
cases.expected_result: On mobile, the first tap reveals the controls overlay while the Live stream keeps playing (video.paused===false) and the central button shows the pause icon — the tap does not toggle playback.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify first tap never pauses the Live stream (accidental-interrupt guard)
preconditions: a 'Live' stream is playing on mobile
steps: Play a Live stream on mobile
Tap the player surface once
Assert: playback state stays playing (no pause)
cases.expected_result: The first tap must NOT pause the stream — a reveal that also toggles playback is the accidental-interrupt regression this story exists to prevent.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify first tap actually reveals the overlay (no-op is a failure)
preconditions: a 'Live' stream is playing on mobile
steps: Play a Live stream on mobile
Tap the player surface once
Assert: the controls overlay is now visible
cases.expected_result: The overlay must actually appear — a first tap that neither reveals nor pauses (a no-op) is a failure.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify tap-outside the button dismisses the overlay and keeps playing
steps: With the overlay visible and playing, tap outside the 64x64px central button
Assert: the overlay dismisses
Assert: playback continues (still playing)
cases.expected_result: Tapping outside the 64x64px central button dismisses the overlay while the Live stream keeps playing — the dismiss is not an implicit pause.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify tap-outside never pauses the stream
steps: Tap outside the central button
Assert: playback state does NOT change to paused
cases.expected_result: A tap-outside that transitions playing → paused is a failure — dismissing the overlay must never pause the stream (BR-10).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the overlay auto-dismisses after 1s of no interaction while playing
steps: Reveal the overlay while playing
Wait 999ms — assert: overlay still visible
Wait to 1000ms with no interaction
Assert: the overlay auto-dismisses and playback continues
cases.expected_result: After exactly 1s (1000ms) of no interaction while playing, the overlay auto-dismisses and playback continues; at 999ms it is still visible.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the overlay is still visible at 999ms (lower boundary)
steps: Reveal the overlay
Wait 999ms with no interaction
Assert: the overlay is still visible
cases.expected_result: At 999ms (just before the 1s boundary) the overlay must still be visible — dismissing before 1s is a boundary failure.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the overlay dismisses at 1000ms, not 3000ms (web 3s→1s regression guard)
steps: Reveal the overlay on web
Wait past 1000ms with no interaction
Assert: the overlay has dismissed by 1000ms (NOT still visible until 3000ms)
cases.expected_result: The overlay must dismiss at 1000ms, not 3000ms — web currently uses a 3s timer (VideoPlayerControls.tsx:60-70); any dismiss later than 1s fails the regression guard.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify pause on a Live stream — play icon persists, no seek, overlay persists, tap-outside stays paused
steps: Tap the central pause button
Assert: playback pauses and the play icon persists
Assert: no ±10s seek buttons are shown
Wait >1s — assert: the paused overlay persists
Tap outside the button — assert: overlay dismisses and stream stays paused
cases.expected_result: On a Live stream the central pause tap pauses playback and the play icon persists; the ±10s seek buttons are never shown; while paused the overlay persists past 1s; a tap-outside dismisses it and the stream stays paused (resume-to-live is UC2).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a recorded/video stream DOES show the ±10s buttons (contrast)
steps: Mock: SDK stream type = recorded / video
Reveal the overlay
Assert: the ±10s skip buttons ARE present
cases.expected_result: Contrast: on a recorded / video stream the ±10s skip buttons ARE present — proving the seek gate is stream-type driven, not always-off (TC-UC1b-01c).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the paused overlay does NOT auto-dismiss on the 1s idle timer
steps: Pause the Live stream
Wait >1s with no interaction
Assert: the paused overlay is still visible (did NOT auto-dismiss)
cases.expected_result: The paused overlay must NOT auto-dismiss on the 1s idle timer — a paused overlay that vanishes after 1s is a BR-11 failure.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify tap-outside while paused never resumes the stream
steps: With the Live stream paused, tap outside the central button
Assert: the overlay dismisses AND the stream stays paused (no resume)
cases.expected_result: A tap-outside while paused must never resume the stream — resume is out of scope here (UC2).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify reveal/dismiss/auto-dismiss/pause are identical across surfaces
preconditions: a 'Live' stream renders on an in-scope surface
steps: Run reveal, tap-outside-dismiss, 1s auto-dismiss, and pause on the inline-feed surface
Repeat on the fullscreen/gallery surface
Assert: the outcomes are identical across both surfaces
cases.expected_result: The reveal / tap-outside-dismiss / 1s auto-dismiss / pause behaviours produce identical outcomes on the inline-feed and fullscreen/gallery surfaces (surface-invariant).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a per-surface behaviour difference is a surface-invariance break
preconditions: a 'Live' stream renders on ≥2 in-scope surfaces
steps: Compare reveal/dismiss/auto-dismiss/pause outcomes across surfaces
Assert: no surface produces a different outcome
cases.expected_result: Any surface producing a DIFFERENT reveal, dismiss, auto-dismiss, or pause outcome than another in-scope surface is a surface-invariance break (BR-06 violation).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify baseline — no overlay before any tap, LIVE badge + viewer count visible
steps: Render an actively-playing Live post without tapping
Assert: no controls overlay is present
Assert: the live video surface, the LIVE badge, and the viewer count are visible
cases.expected_result: On first render of an actively-playing Live post with no tap, no controls overlay is present — only the live video surface, the standing LIVE badge, and the viewer count are visible (baseline S0).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify no overlay is rendered before any interaction
steps: Render the Live post without tapping
Assert: the controls overlay is absent from the DOM/tree
cases.expected_result: The controls overlay must NOT be present before any tap — an overlay rendered pre-interaction is a baseline-state failure.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a control interaction restarts the 1s auto-dismiss countdown
steps: Reveal the overlay
Interact with a control at 800ms
Assert: the overlay is still visible past the original 1000ms
Assert: it auto-dismisses only 1000ms after the interaction
cases.expected_result: A control interaction at 800ms restarts the 1s countdown — the overlay stays visible past the original 1000ms and auto-dismisses only 1000ms after the last interaction.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the countdown does not ignore a later interaction
preconditions: an interaction occurred after the reveal
steps: Reveal the overlay, interact at 800ms
Assert: the overlay does NOT dismiss at 1000ms-after-reveal (the timer restarted on the interaction)
cases.expected_result: If the overlay dismisses 1000ms after the FIRST reveal (ignoring the later interaction) the countdown-reset failed — the timer must restart on every control interaction.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a pause tap at the auto-dismiss instant — pause wins
preconditions: the 1s idle timer is about to fire
steps: Let the 1s idle timer reach the firing instant
Tap the central pause button at that exact instant
Assert: state becomes paused, the play icon persists, and the overlay is not swallowed by the expiring timer
Assert: the overlay dismisses only on a later tap-outside
cases.expected_result: When the pause tap lands at the exact instant the 1s auto-dismiss fires, the explicit pause wins: state becomes paused, the play icon persists, and the overlay is not swallowed by the expiring timer — it dismisses only on a later tap-outside.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the expiring timer does not swallow the pause
steps: Fire the pause tap at the auto-dismiss instant
Assert: the overlay does not auto-dismiss losing the paused/play-icon state, and the stream does not stay playing
cases.expected_result: The expiring timer must not swallow the pause — a race where the overlay auto-dismisses and the paused / play-icon state is lost (or the stream stays playing) is the failure mode.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify tap during buffering reveals the overlay with the real state (no false play icon)
preconditions: the 'Live' stream is buffering (not yet playing)
steps: Force the Live stream into a buffering state
Tap the player surface
Assert: the overlay appears with the central button reflecting the real buffering state (not a false 'playing' pause-icon)
Assert: no crash and no frozen overlay
cases.expected_result: Tapping the player while the Live stream is buffering reveals the overlay with the central button reflecting the real buffering state — never a false 'playing' pause-icon — with no crash and no frozen overlay.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a mid-play stall surfaces an explicit buffering/Reconnecting state [AI-INFERRED]
preconditions: the 'Live' stream was playing, then the network stalls
steps: Play the Live stream, then stall the network mid-play
Assert: an explicit buffering / 'Reconnecting' state surfaces (never a silent frozen frame)
cases.expected_result: [AI-INFERRED] Mid-play stall: an explicit buffering / 'Reconnecting' state must surface — the viewer is never left on a silent frozen frame (BR-15). (paused-reconnect is UC2.)

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the central button never shows a false 'playing' icon while buffering
steps: Force buffering
Reveal the overlay
Assert: the central button reflects the buffering/loading state, never a 'playing' pause-icon
cases.expected_result: The central button must never show a false 'playing' pause-icon while the stream is buffering — the state must reflect reality.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify backgrounding during an active overlay/timer resolves to the OS-default state
steps: Reveal the overlay/timer, then background the app for >1s
Return to foreground
Assert: a well-defined state via the OS default — no stale mid-countdown overlay, no implicit play/pause toggle beyond the OS default
cases.expected_result: Backgrounding the app for >1s while the overlay/timer is active and returning to foreground yields a well-defined state via the OS default — no stale mid-countdown overlay and no implicit play/pause toggle beyond the OS default.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify no stale overlay or implicit toggle after foreground
steps: Background with the overlay active, then foreground
Assert: no stale mid-countdown overlay remains and no implicit play/pause toggle beyond the OS default occurred
cases.expected_result: A stale mid-countdown overlay left on screen after foreground, or an implicit play/pause toggle beyond the OS default, is the failure mode.

cases.name: [Live player] Observe Live foreground snap-to-live (UC2 behaviour — do NOT assert)
steps: Background then foreground a Live stream
Observe whether playback snaps toward the live edge
Record the observation — do NOT assert (this is UC2's behaviour)
cases.expected_result: OBSERVE/RECORD ONLY — Live foreground snap-to-live is UC2's behaviour; observed here, never asserted.
